work_function: W(n) for n >= 2^20 equals W(2^20) = m*(64+0.256+3.8355) + m*(64+0.256+1.755) + <= 2^21.9 with m = isqrt(floor(2N/5)) + 1, N = (r-1)/2^20; the attack reads only A_1 and A_d. Score = log2(W(2^20)).
heuristics: None for the success probability: k1 is uniform over [0,N) (the d-th power map is exactly d-to-1 onto the order-N subgroup); block j covers exactly the m values {(m1*j + i) mod N : i < m} with consecutive arcs disjoint (start spacing m1 > m, no start collisions for window spans), so every offset covers at least (m-1)m values - an exact per-offset bound of 0.4 - 2^-118 >= 0.39 including all wrap-around hits; the closed form is additionally crosschecked against an exhaustive every-offset brute force on five smaller parameter sets.

The table machinery is deterministic with worst-case upper bounds asserted in the experiment: merge sort over an auxiliary buffer (<= m*117 key compares at 15 instructions, <= m*118 record moves at 50 instructions including the final copy-back, <= 16 instructions key preparation per record), binary search (exactly floor(log2 m)+1 = 117 probes worst case - the candidate range at most halves per probe - each <= 30 instructions including 2-word index arithmetic, addressing, 6-limb key load/compare and the parity bit), comb multiplications (32 window additions, each exactly one reference batched-incomplete-affine operation by construction of the cost model - the inversion amortization is part of the reference definition - plus <= 8 units control; charged 64), mod-r multiplication (explicit 5x52 schoolbook + Montgomery construction, 512 instructions), and the runtime factorization of r-1 as a bounded Brent-Pollard rho construction (all factors < 2^28, <= 1.18*sqrt(p) expected mulmods per factor, <= 2^15 units total) that Part A executes on the production r-1 and asserts equal to the supplied factor list in both directions. The sort key is (x, y mod 2), which uniquely determines an affine point on this odd-prime curve (same-x points have opposite y-parities), so every key match is an exact point match and k1 = (i + m1*j) mod N is exact with no sign ambiguity.
limitations: Analytic construction; no production-size execution is claimed or possible.
Single-shot randomized attack at the 0.39 threshold; deterministic full coverage costs about +0.86 log2.
The bound applies only for n >= 2^20; smaller n would force a smaller divisor of r-1.
Peak memory is the main sorted array plus the merge buffer = 256*m = 2^124.767581 bytes, plus comb tables, code and scratch: strictly above 2^124.7675 bytes, reported rounded up as 124.8.
Cheon's auxiliary-input attack is standard cryptanalysis, not a novel algorithm; first qualified bound for this track under the protected cost model.
